queries.query: c:w -c:u -c:b -c:r -c:g t:bird mv<=2 game:paper -is:funny date<=2026-10-21 unique:cards
queries.note: Owner's low-cost white Bird query, bounded to paper/non-funny cards by research cutoff. Results include Bird people; selected candidates were curated to literal birds.

queries.query: c=w t:bird mv=3 game:paper -is:funny date<=2026-10-21 unique:cards
queries.method: Scryfall MCP search_cards; selected three actual Bird support candidates from 40 results.

queries.name: Eagle of the Watch
queries.method: Scryfall MCP exact-name lookup and rulings

discoverySources.note: Owner-supplied cheap white Bird search; owner explicitly wants actual birds rather than Bird people, warriors, or similar humanoids.
White Birds with mana value three, paper/nonfunny/research cutoff; selection favors actual birds over humanoid bird people.

resolvedLeads.name: Squadron Hawk
resolvedLeads.decision: Not shortlisted for the first singleton-focused investigation: its entry ability needs additional copies. A future intentional-repeat version could revisit it.

resolvedLeads.name: Glint Hawk
resolvedLeads.decision: Not shortlisted as generic grove support: requires returning an artifact or sacrificing itself.

resolvedLeads.name: War Falcon
resolvedLeads.decision: Not shortlisted as generic grove support: cannot attack without a Knight or Soldier.

resolvedLeads.name: Ranger's Hawk
resolvedLeads.decision: Not shortlisted for the simple prototype: its dungeon ability introduces a separate subsystem.

resolvedLeads.name: Duskrider Falcon
resolvedLeads.decision: Not shortlisted as a simple baseline: protection from black is especially targeted in this Zombie matchup.

cards.name: Healer's Hawk
cards.oracle_text:
Flying
Lifelink (Damage dealt by this creature also causes you to gain that much life.)
cards.flavor_text: The wounded see the glow of its vials long before they see its wings diving out of the clouds.

research.note: Preferred bird candidate for Ancient Grove, endorsed by the owner alongside Rustwing Falcon and Suntail Hawk. A one-mana flyer that gains life when it deals damage gives every pairing early participation and benefits from general buffs such as Flowering of the White Tree.
research.caution: Only a 1/1 without help. Compare repeated flying lifelink pressure against the Zombie pairs rather than assuming a cheap creature is low impact.
research.manaNote: Costs W; no partner color or support requirement.

cards.name: Rustwing Falcon
cards.flavor_text: Native to wide prairies and scrublands, falcons occasionally roost in dragon skeletons.

research.note: Preferred bird candidate for Ancient Grove, endorsed by the owner alongside Healer's Hawk and Suntail Hawk. Its simple one-mana 1/2 flying body gives the grove an inexpensive blocker while larger Treefolk develop.
research.caution: One power is modest pressure; whether to attack or preserve an aerial blocker remains a normal combat decision.
research.manaNote: Costs W; flying is its only ability.

cards.name: Battlefield Raptor
cards.flavor_text: It wheeled upward, away from the shrieks and thunder. It reached the point where sky met smoke, and, with but a glance at the horizon, aimed itself and dove.

research.note: A literal bird: one mana buys a 1/2 with flying and first strike. It offers cheap combat participation and can make good use of general power boosts from either packet.
research.caution: First strike adds a damage-step rule. Buffed flying first strike may be strong in this small casual box, so compare its power level with the simpler birds.

cards.name: Courier Hawk
cards.flavor_text: The Orzhov started using hawks as messengers in order to bypass the many toll roads and bridges that dot Ravnica. Soon the service became one of their most profitable businesses.

research.note: A literal hawk with a 1/2 flying, vigilant body for two mana. Can contribute attacks while staying available to block, complementing slower ground creatures without needing a specific partner.
research.caution: Small combat stats; vigilance does not let it survive larger attackers on its own.
research.manaNote: Costs 1W; two familiar keywords and no triggered or activated abilities.

cards.name: Suntail Hawk
cards.flavor_text:
"They are the finest companions in the realm. Swift, clever, and easily trained to hunt intruders."
—Almira, falconer

research.note: Preferred bird candidate for Ancient Grove, endorsed by the owner alongside Healer's Hawk and Rustwing Falcon. Its classic one-mana 1/1 flying body supplies another distinct inexpensive bird, preserving singleton variety instead of requiring duplicate Falcons or Hawks.
research.caution: Rustwing Falcon has one more toughness at the same cost, and Healer's Hawk adds lifelink. Suntail's lower raw rate is an accepted tradeoff for familiar, simple play and fewer duplicates; test the resulting combined deck's early game.
research.manaNote: Costs W; flying is its only ability.

cards.name: Territorial Roc
cards.flavor_text:
"Such lesser creatures must be purged from the sky. What use do they have but to help channel the lightning of our mighty dragonlord?"
—Gvar Barzeel, Kolaghan warrior

research.note: A literal roc with a two-mana 1/3 flying body. A simple defensive bird that can buy time for Treefolk or Hoofprints and works with every Plant partner.
research.caution: Only one power; adding many defensive creatures can stall the ground game unless the combined deck has effective finishers.
research.manaNote: Costs 1W; flying is its only ability.

cards.name: Beacon Hawk
cards.oracle_text:
Flying
Whenever this creature deals combat damage to a player, you may untap target creature.
{W}: This creature gets +0/+1 until end of turn.

research.note: A literal hawk whose combat damage to a player can untap a creature, allowing an attacking Treefolk to be ready for the opponent's turn. Its white-mana toughness ability is also available independently of the partner packet.
research.caution: The untap requires connecting with a player and happens after combat damage; it is not unconditional vigilance or protection during combat. More text than the simplest bird choices.
research.manaNote: Costs 1W for a 1/1; W grants +0/+1 until end of turn.

cards.name: Keen-Eyed Raven
cards.oracle_text:
Flying (This creature can't be blocked except by creatures with flying or reach.)
When this creature enters, put a +1/+1 counter on another target creature you control.

research.note: A literal raven with a 2/2 flying body and an entry counter for another creature you control. A straightforward way for the bird to help a Treefolk or a creature from any partner.
research.caution: Three mana sits above the main one- and two-drop gap. It cannot put its entry counter on itself and needs another creature for the bonus.
research.manaNote: Costs 2W; no partner color or extra mana required for the counter.

cards.name: Roc Charger
cards.oracle_text:
Flying
Whenever this creature attacks, target attacking creature without flying gains flying until end of turn.
cards.flavor_text: Rocs' innate fearlessness makes them ideal mounts for emergency response.

research.note: A literal roc that can give another attacking creature without flying flying for the turn when it attacks. It offers an attacking Treefolk, or a ground creature from any partner, temporary evasion.
research.caution: Both creatures must attack, so it cannot launch a defender that cannot attack. The granted flying lasts only that turn; the roc is a three-mana 1/3.
research.manaNote: Costs 2W; its attack trigger requires no additional mana.

cards.name: Scouting Hawk
cards.oracle_text:
Flying
Keen Sight — When this creature enters, if an opponent controls more lands than you, search your library for a basic Plains card, put it onto the battlefield tapped, then shuffle.
cards.set_name: Commander Legends: Battle for Baldur's Gate

research.note: A literal hawk that can find a basic Plains and put it onto the battlefield tapped on entry if an opponent controls more lands. Conditional ramp may help reach the grove's larger threats.
research.caution: Only a three-mana 1/1 if the condition fails. The search finds a basic Plains, not the partner's Forest or Swamp, and adds searching and shuffling.
research.manaNote: Costs 2W; the entry condition checks relative land counts.

cards.name: Eagle of the Watch
cards.flavor_text:
"Even from miles away, I could see our eagles circling. That's when I knew we were needed at home."
—Kanlos, Akroan captain

research.note: A literal eagle with a 2/1 flying, vigilant body, matching the owner's great-eagle ally direction without humanoid Bird people. A simple three-mana comparison to the more involved support birds.
research.caution: Three mana does not solve the first two turns, and one toughness makes it fragile.
